newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe suspends private phone decision.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe suspends private phone decision.

text.p: Zimbabwe's state tender board has suspended a controversial decision by the government to award the country's first private cellular phone licence to a consortium of black businesses and a Zairean-based company following an appeal by a losing local bidder.

The board said in a statement on Friday the Information, Posts and Telecommunications Ministry should in the next three weeks, reply "point by point" to complaints lodged by bidder Econet against the award of the licence to Telecel.
"By virtue of this appeal, action on TBR 4317B (cellular phone tender award) of 5 March 1997 is automatically suspended until the appeal is cleared," tender board chairman Stanley Mahlala said.

Econet, which has been involved in court battles for the past three years to win a licence to operate the southern African country's first private cellular telephone service, this week alleged that the tender process was rigged in favour of Telecel.
On Thursday, two other losing contenders, Tritel and Supanet, added their complaints to Econet's and said they were seeking legal advice on the issue.
Econet, Tritel and Supanet spurned an offer from the government that they take a 15-20 percent equity stake in Telecel's project which was scheduled to start service in eight months.

"Our review of the winning bid has raised fundamental questions on the adjudication process that will require consultations with our legal counsel before making our position on the tender process public," Tritel and Supanet said in a statement on Thursday.
Tritel's Christopher Mutsvangwa alleged that Telecel's bid failed to comply with the tender requirements in key aspects, describing its financial bid as "meaningless".
